title: PCIe retrain ↔ ECC burst correlation — nightshift notes & runbook draft
body:
Context and why I wrote this
- Nightshift (2026-04-12 23:10–02:40 UTC) we observed 4 short GPU outages on cluster-edge-03 that coincided with short-lived ECC soft error spikes and simultaneous PCIe link retrains reported in kernel logs. This doc collects the raw observations, quick mitigation that kept nodes online, and a provisional runbook for oncall when we see PCIe retrain + ECC bursts.

High-level hypothesis (working)
- Hypothesis A: Transient power/voltage jitter on a subset of boards causes memory subsystem errors (soft ECC) and also triggers the PCIe link to retrain (or the reverse).
- Hypothesis B: A driver/firmware path triggers link state transitions under heavy DMA patterns, and that transient state increases memory read retries visible as ECC soft counts.
- Hypothesis C: Intermittent thermal/clock gating edge case on firmware that leads to both symptoms.

What we observed (raw signals)
- Kernel dmesg snippets (times are UTC):
  - 2026-04-12T23:11:02Z: "pcieport 0000:03:00.0: AER: Root Port detected a fatal error: Multiple AER errors"
  - 2026-04-12T23:11:02Z: "GPU0: ECC: 34 soft corrected errors on channel 2"
  - 2026-04-12T23:11:03Z: "nvidia: GPU reset required; resetting device"
  - 2026-04-13T00:26:15Z: "pcieport 0000:03:00.0: link retrain request" then ECC spike + driver reset
- Prometheus metrics (node exporter + nv_peer):
  - node_gpu_ecc_soft_count increased by ~40 over 30s at each event
  - node_pcie_corrected_errors counter increments (small spikes) co-temporal with ECC spikes
  - no sustained temperature increase in host sensors (CPU/GPU therms within normal bounds)
- Telemetry gaps/missing: PCIe per-lane counters are not currently scraped; we only have platform-level AER counters. No BMC logs were preserved for one incident due to BMC reboot.

Immediate actions taken during incident
- Disabled preemption-heavy workload (inference batch jobs) on the node pool (moved jobs to dedicated-ready nodes).
- Applied a temporary nv driver parameter (nvidia.NVreg_RegistryDwords="OverrideNvVBIOS=1") ??? (we tried conservative param flip from staging guide) — note: this is experimental and reverted next day.
- Forced node reboot when we saw repeated resets in < 5 minutes to avoid cascading flapping.
- Opened a ticket with board vendor and attached dmesg and ECC delta logs.

Why this is tricky for oncall
- Symptoms are short-lived and noisy (ECC soft counts can spike for many benign reasons).
- Driver resets can mask underlying PCIe/AER root cause (we see "GPU reset" messages but that is often a symptom).
- Eviction / autoscaler behavior on repeated resets can surface customer impact quickly.

Provisional detection rules (for alerting)
- New alert: pcie_retrain_and_ecc_burst_alert (severity: P2) triggers if all three are true within 60s:
  1) node_gpu_ecc_soft_count delta >= 20 in 60s
  2) node_pcie_retrain_events delta >= 1 in 60s (AER link retrain flag)
  3) nvidia_driver_reset_count delta >= 1 in 60s
- Rationale: requires correlation to avoid noisy ECC-only alerts.

Triage checklist (provisional runbook steps for oncall)
1) Triage entry
  - Check alert page -> identify node(s), times.
  - Pull last 10 minutes of dmesg and /var/log/messages.
  - Pull nvml logs and nv_peer exporter dump: "nvidia-smi -q -d ECC,RETURNS" and our exporter endpoint (/metrics).
2) Quick containment (if customer impact or repeated resets)
  - Cordon the node in k8s: kubectl cordon <node>
  - Drain with gentle termination: kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120
  - If node flapping is < 3 resets in 10 minutes, safer option: limit affinity and reschedule heavy GPU batch jobs off that node via nodeSelector/taints.
3) Collect diagnostics (before reboot when possible)
  - Copy dmesg tail and journalctl -k --since "15 minutes ago" to /tmp/incident-<id>/logs
  - Run: setpci -s 03:00.0 CAP_EXP+0x18.L (get link status) and lspci -vvv -s 03:00.0
  - Dump AER status: cat /sys/kernel/debug/pcie/0000:03:00.0/aer_log (if available)
  - Dump ECC counters: nvidia-smi --query-gpu=ecc.errors.uncorrected.ecc, ecc.errors.corrected.ecc --format=csv
  - If BMC is reachable: ipmitool sel list; get system event logs.
4) Short mitigation options (pick one):
  - Option A (soft): bump power cap down by 10% for node via dcgmi/powerMgt or vendor tool to reduce transient rail load (useful if we suspect power jitter).
  - Option B (driver): if running an older driver and vendor suggests, try staged driver with known PCIe/AER fixes on a sacrificial node only.
  - Option C (firmware): coordinate with vendor to schedule vBIOS/firmware update (longer path).
5) Escalation
  - If resets continue after containment or vendor asks: page electronics team and hardware vendor support (INFR-3784).
  - If multiple racks/nodes show identical pattern, treat as P1 and involve infra-eng and SRE leads.

Longer-term action items (post-incident)
- Instrumentation: add PCIe lane-level counters to exporter and scrape AER logs to Prom for per-node timelines.
- Owner: Diego A. — add metrics to node exporter and add dashboard tile.
- Run controlled experiments: create canary nodes with driver X and firmware Y and run stress patterns that replicate DMA load. Record when retrain occurs.
- Vendor engagement: request detailed board power-rail telemetry and check for recent BMC firmware updates (we saw 2 nodes with old BMC in this fleet).
- Autoscaler behavior: add a cooldown window for node eviction when GPU resets are <3 in 10 minutes to avoid aggressive churn.

Notes / ideas encountered during nightshift
- We noticed that retrains often happened ~2–3s after a large DMA burst from userside process (inference batch flush). Could be a corner-case with the driver's DMA ring wrap handling.
- BMC SEL had repeated "PSOK lost" warnings on one node — vendor suspects a power sequencing issue during peak draws.
- Consider a low-risk test: throttle PCIe link speed to Gen3 (if currently Gen4) on test nodes and see whether retrain frequency drops. This can be toggled via setpci in many platforms (but must be validated on the specific board).

Open questions (for postmortem)
- Is the sequence always: DMA burst -> link retrain -> ECC spike -> driver reset? Or are there cases where ECC counts precede link retrain?
- Is there any correlation with host kernel updates? We upgraded kernel on a subset of nodes 2026-03-28.
- Are BMC reboots masking telemetry? Need to harden SEL retention and log forwarding.

Action items assigned (short)
- Diego Alvarez: add PCIe/AER scrape + dashboard (ETA 2 weeks).
- Priya Singh: schedule vendor call and collect BMC logs for nodes identified in INFR-3784 (ETA 3 days).
- Noah Patel: test controlled driver variant on sacrificial canary node and run synthetic DMA stress (ETA 1 week).
- Maya Chen (me): convert this note into postmortem skeleton and set up shared timeline doc, add links to ticket and dmesg snippets (ETA 48h).

Appendix — quick commands cheat-sheet for oncall
- dmesg grep: dmesg --ctime | egrep -i "pcie|aer|ecc|nvidia|reset" | tail -n 200
- nv dump: nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,temperature.gpu,driver_model,clocks.gr,clocks.sm,ecc.errors.corrected.volatile --format=csv -l 1
- pcie info: lspci -s 03:00.0 -vvv ; setpci -s 03:00.0 0x80.l ; cat /sys/kernel/debug/pcie/0000:03:00.0/aer_log
- BMC: ipmitool -I lanplus -H <bmc> -U admin sel list ; ipmitool sel elist

Closing note
- This is a working draft intended for oncall nightshift teams. The correlation rule above has been pushed to staging alerts and will be tested for one week to tune thresholds. Please append any logs you collect to the Confluence incident timeline page and ping in #sre-gpu for real-time help.
